This directory is completely empty, so there's no existing change-record template or system for me to populate — I'll need you to point me at the right format/location (e.g., a specific file, ticketing system, or template).

Before I fill it in, one thing needs nailing down: **does CI build #9012 correspond to the commit SHA after your rebase, or before it?** You rebased last night and re-pushed, which creates a new commit even though the file diff is unchanged. If build #9012 ran on the pre-rebase commit, then "CI is green, 340 tests passed" isn't actually evidence for the code that will be deployed — it never ran against the merged state that includes yesterday's queue-timeout fix. Given retry backoff and queue timeout are both timing-related, that interaction is exactly the kind of thing a stale CI run would miss.

Same question for Priya's approval — GitHub review approvals are sometimes dismissed on force-push depending on branch protection settings, so I'd want to know whether she approved the pre- or post-rebase SHA.

Can you confirm:
1. The commit SHA build #9012 ran against, and that it matches your current branch HEAD
2. Whether Priya's approval is still attached to that same SHA (or she re-approved after the rebase)

Once I have that, I'll draft the record with the actual verified evidence rather than just restating the claim. If it turns out CI hasn't re-run on the rebased commit, the honest move is to trigger a fresh CI run before 5pm rather than merge on stale evidence — that's a few minutes, not a blocker to your window.
